transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-30
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Owen Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood CSM), Lena Ortiz (Tideway - Head ML Ops), Rajiv Menon (Tideway - Platform), Sofia Alvarez (Tideway - Security), Markus Lee (Tideway - SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Renewal discussion focused on contract rollforward and small uplift for APAC nodes.
- Customer wants APAC edge activation, SOC2/KMS confirmation, and a short perf pilot.
- Pricing worksheet and pilot runbook to be exchanged; next steps agreed.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone thanks for joining on a Friday, um small agenda - renewal framing, APAC edge activation, security checklist, and then pilot logistics. How's that sound?
00:12 Speaker 2 (Lena): Sounds good, Maya. Quick note we had an exec sync this morning, leadership wants clarity on cost posture and latency before they sign-off.
00:20 Maya: Totally, totally understood. Diego and Owen from my side will cover the perf/pilot bits. Owen will walk through what the APAC nodes look like.
00:33 Owen: Hi all - brief from me, we propose scoped APAC edge nodes in singapore and sydney, with optional burst capacity to mainland APAC. We'll run a 48-hour perf pilot against a sample workload to validate p95 under expected spike scenarios.
00:48 Rajiv: Quick Q - are the APAC nodes dedicated or shared? We're trying to figure isolation and also predictability for latency.
00:55 Owen: Good question. We have two flavors: Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) or Shared hosted with region affinity. Dedicated gives nailed-down throughput and lower jitter, hosted is cheaper but can have variable tail latency.
01:10 Lena: Leadership is leaning dedicated because of customer-facing SLAs; cost is secondary but still important.
01:18 Maya: Ok noted. We'll show committed options and hybrid—dedicated baseline plus burst on hosted for overflow.
01:26 Sofia: From security we're mainly checking encryption at rest/in transit, KMS integration, and audit logs. Also SSO and SCIM for access provisioning.
01:36 Diego: We already have the SOC2 report on file, we'll re-share; also we can provide KMS integration notes.
01:42 Sofia: When you say KMS integration - is Redwood supporting customer-managed keys (CMK) or is it service-managed?
01:50 Owen: For private customers we support CMK via standard KMS/HSM integration; for hosted API customers there's an option for envelope encryption with customer keys in supported clouds. I'll pull examples in the doc.
02:05 Markus: Any egress charge surprises we should be aware of when routing traffic cross-region? We need to model cost for multi-region failover.
02:12 Maya: Good call. We'll include estimated egress and compute cost delta for cross-region fallback in the pricing sheet.
02:19 Rajiv: Also, curious about prefix/KV cache behavior when you run a canary rollout across regions. Will the cache warm-up be a penalty?
02:30 Owen: There is a warm-up - prefix cache is regional and uses local KV cache; we can pre-warm using a synthetic trace in pilot to reduce cold-start overhead. We'll include a pre-warm script.
02:44 Lena: Ok that's helpful. On contract: we're looking at a 12-month rollforward with a modest 20% uplift in committed capacity for Q3/Q4, plus the APAC edge add-on.
02:56 Maya: Great — we'll model a few commitment tiers: 0% uplift (baseline renewal), 20% uplift (recommended), and a 40% uplift for discounted pricing. Each model will include dedicated node options.
03:10 Sofia: For compliance, we need retention windows and log exportability. Can you surface where audit logs are stored and how long?
03:19 Diego: Audit logs are retained in the control plane for 90 days by default, longer retention is an add-on; we can push an export to your S3 bucket or a SIEM via webhook.
03:30 Sofia: We'll want an architecture diagram showing the private control plane and data paths for APAC nodes.
03:36 Owen: I'll attach a diagram in the follow-up, but short answer: control plane in our US region with region-specific serving nodes; customer traffic is pinned regionally per policy.
03:48 Markus: Does private deployment (VPC/on-prem) change the KMS story? We have a downstream team looking at onprem options.
03:56 Owen: On-prem packages support local HSM and direct KMS integrations; it's more hands-on but gets you full key control and no cross-region egress for keys.
04:09 Lena: We have a mixed strategy: most traffic stays on hosted, but for regulated clients we'll need private nodes in region. So the ask is a clear path and rough cost for private node pilot in SG.
04:21 Maya: Understood. We'll put a private-onprem pilot estimate specifically for SG with timelines for procurement and infra.
04:29 Rajiv: Timeline — leadership expects a decision by mid-May. We need a pilot before sign-off ideally. So can we schedule the pilot week of 2026-05-10?
04:39 Diego: That's doable. Owen and Markus can run a short 48-72 hour pilot that includes: warm-up traces, load tests, and KV cache observations.
04:51 Markus: For the perf pilot, we'll also want an A/B comparison to our current self-hosted setup. Can you mirror model versions/quantization?
05:00 Owen: We can match model variant and quantization level; we'll capture tokenization and seed prompts to make the comparison fair. There might be small differences in kernel implementations but we'll annotate those in the runbook.
05:15 Lena: Pricing specifics — the exec wants a clear monthly delta for the 20% uplift + APAC edge. The current contract renewal is on the table on June 15, so we need numbers early May.
05:27 Maya: We'll prioritize the pricing worksheet; you should have it by 2026-05-03.
05:33 Rajiv: Any risk of capacity being unavailable in APAC at peak? If reserved nodes are provisioned, how long until they're live?
05:42 Maya: Provisioning reserved pools in APAC typically takes 3-5 business days after contract sign and capacity allocation; for pilot we can use pre-provisioned test pools to speed things up.
05:54 Sofia: Legal — any changes to data residency clauses with APAC nodes? We need to confirm where logs and model artifacts reside.
06:02 Diego: Data residency depends on deployment mode. Hosted region nodes keep transient KV cache and token generation in-region, but control plane metadata might flow to the US control plane. For private deployments we can localize control plane. We'll add a residency matrix to the follow-up.
06:20 Lena: Ok thanks. I want to flag one more thing — we had a recent P0 where p99 spiked during a promo, so we want to see p95 and p99 in the pilot.
06:29 Owen: We'll capture p50/p95/p99, tail latency, and token-per-second metrics. Also we'll measure cost-per-token under load.
06:39 Markus: Do you have guidance on batching that balances cost and latency? Our app is latency-sensitive for auth flows.
06:47 Owen: Yes - for auth flows you probably want single-request low-latency path with minimal batching; for async flows batching is useful. We'll include suggested batching/quantization profiles per route.
06:57 Lena: Noted. On security documentation, what format will the SOC2/KMS docs be in? We need an auditable artifact.
07:05 Diego: SOC2 we can share the report PDF; for KMS we'll share a short architecture diagram plus the key rotation policy and HSM vendor notes.
07:15 Sofia: Please mask any customer names in the SOC2 PDF before sharing.
07:19 Diego: Ack. We'll scrub and share via secure link.
07:23 Maya: Quick commercial question - if Tideway wants a staged rollout across APAC, do we have a discount for multi-region commitments?
07:31 Maya: (continuing) Typically yes, we provide incremental discounts at certain commitment thresholds and multi-region bundles – I'll show a 2-region and 3-region bundle in pricing.
07:43 Rajiv: About observability: can we get token-level cost breakdowns per route for chargeback?
07:49 Owen: Yes - Redwood Console gives per-route token costs and latency histograms. For customers on Dedicated we can increase retention and export to your billing system.
07:59 Lena: Great. Anything else on the pilot instrumentation?
08:04 Owen: We'll include tracing hooks (open-telemetry) and example dashboards.
08:09 Lena: Ok, then let's talk dates and deliverables recap.
08:12 Maya: Recap — Redwood will: 1) send updated pricing + SOW by 2026-05-03; 2) share SOC2 doc and KMS diagram by 2026-05-04; 3) Owen to prepare pilot runbook and pre-warm script by 2026-05-07; 4) schedule pilot kickoff week of 2026-05-10. Tideway will: provide token histograms and spike windows (due 2026-05-05), confirm internal stakeholders for pilot, and review pricing.
08:40 Lena: That matches our notes. We'll aim to have decision mid-May.
08:46 Sofia: One more compliance ask — can we get a short note on encryption key rotation frequency and support for customer-managed rotation?
08:55 Owen: Yes, we'll include key rotation cadence and examples for CMK rotation.
09:00 Maya: Perfect. Any blockers?
09:03 Rajiv: None; just timing. If we get the pricing early we can push to leadership.
09:08 Maya: Great. I'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite. Diego will set the pilot invite.
09:14 Diego: I'll send invites after the call - proposing May 11th for a kickoff.
09:19 Lena: May 11th works tentatively.
09:22 Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll close with action items and share the drive links.
09:26 (call ends)
